chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Adhan is shortened during travel just as the prayer is shortened; the Adhan is called out one by one, and the Iqamah is called out one by one.
ai.seo_question: How are the Adhan and Iqamah shortened during travel in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Reported from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the procedural aspect of *Qasr* (shortening prayers) by extending the principle of reduction to the Adhan and Iqamah. It establishes that during travel, each phrase of the call is recited once rather than twice, ensuring consistency between the ritual call and the shortened four-rak'ah prayer. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on maintaining the structural integrity of worship even when concessions for ease are applied.
